sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Collierville?
sections.html:
Collierville owners deal with two taxing bodies, the Town of Collierville and Shelby County. The town's tax department takes questions at 901-457-2281 or propertytax@colliervilletn.gov, and its Taxes page notes that residents also owe county tax.

Within the county system, the Assessor of Property establishes value, the Board of Commissioners picks the county rate, and the Trustee prints notices and mails them to whatever address the Assessor holds. Where a lender escrows your taxes, the servicer may ask for the figures and pay, and the Trustee advises borrowers to hold on to the original notice anyway.

Since the notice follows the Assessor's mailing address, someone who has moved should update it well before October.

sections.h2: What is the Collierville tax rate and how is a bill figured?
sections.html:
The town's Taxes page gives its rate as $1.62 for each $100 of assessed value. Tennessee assesses homes at 25% of appraisal, so a $100,000 house is $25,000 on the roll and owes $405.00 to the town.

The same page also lists 40% for commercial and industrial parcels, 55% for public utilities, 25% for farms and 30% for personal property. The Trustee or the Assessor can tell you the Shelby County rate to add on top. Using the Census Bureau's $485,900 median owner-occupied value as a sample house, assessed value is $121,475 and the town share lands near $1,968.

sections.h2: When are Collierville property taxes due and when do they go delinquent?
sections.html:
Shelby County taxes open on the first Monday of October and stay interest-free until the end of February. With today being November 15, 2026, the current bill is payable now, and the interest-free period ends in February 2027.

The Trustee's interest page puts Collierville in the group whose bills turn delinquent March 1. Unpaid base tax then gains 1.5% a month, which the Trustee states as 18% a year. A mailed check counts when postmarked by the final day of February, and the stub of your notice goes with it to the Shelby County Trustee, P.O. Box 2751, Memphis, TN 38101-2751.

Call Trustee customer service at (901) 222-0200 with account questions. Under Tenn. Code Ann. 67-5-2405 the Trustee must sue to collect delinquent real estate tax, and a tax lien stays until the full balance is paid.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Collierville assessment?
sections.html:
The first stop is an informal review with the Shelby County Assessor, followed by a Board of Equalization filing if you still disagree. The Assessor stresses that an informal review is not an appeal. It lets you hand over information so the value tracks the market.

Where a Collierville value dispute goes next
StepTimingWhere
Informal reviewCloses on the last day of MayShelby County Assessor of Property
County board appealTypically closes the last working day of JuneBoard of Equalization, 901-222-7300
State board appealAugust 1, or 45 days following the county notice if that is laterState Board of Equalization, 615-401-7883
CourtFinal stepShelby County Chancery Court

Sources: Shelby County Assessor, Appeals Process and the state assessment schedule. The 2026 deadlines are behind us, so a new dispute belongs to the 2027 cycle.

sections.h2: What documents help in a Collierville value dispute?
sections.html:
The Assessor wants proof that points to market value. Useful exhibits for a Collierville house:

  • Nearby sale prices of comparable homes from the two years before the tax year at issue.
  • A private appraisal done recently.
  • Interior and exterior photographs showing condition.
  • For income property, three years of income and expense records.

The Census Bureau puts the typical owner-occupied value at $485,900 for 2020 to 2024, with 79.9% of units occupied by owners. One median hides a wide spread, so lean on sales from your own neighborhood.

sections.h2: What does Collierville look like for a home seller?
sections.html:
The town had about 51,909 people in the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate and sits in the Memphis metropolitan area, with its own district, Collierville Schools. The 2020 count was 51,324, against 43,965 ten years earlier.

Jesse R. Collier laid out the settlement in 1836, and the town was rechartered in 1870 after Civil War damage. The old downtown around the square is a listed historic district. Interstate 269, State Route 385 and Poplar Avenue carry most of the traffic.

Census QuickFacts describes local households this way for 2020 to 2024:

  • 18,161 households averaging 2.82 people.
  • Median household income of $138,598.
  • Median gross rent of $1,691.
  • 62.5% of residents over 25 with a four-year degree or more.
  • An average commute of 25.1 minutes.

Source: Census QuickFacts.

sections.h2: Does Collierville's climate and layout matter to a buyer?
sections.html:
Summers in Collierville run hot and damp, winters stay mild, and the town gets roughly 55 inches of rain annually. Wikipedia's climate summary adds that spring brings the most thunderstorms, hail and tornadoes, with local tornado activity above the Tennessee average.

The Census Bureau counts 36.32 square miles of land and about 1,413 residents per square mile. Buyers tend to ask about the roof and storm history, so gather those records before listing.

sections.h2: Who lives in Collierville besides the tax-bill payers?
sections.html:
QuickFacts shows a family-heavy town. About 26.8% of residents are under 18 and 16.0% are 65 or older, while 97.8% of households subscribe to broadband and 99.0% have a computer. The town counts 2,189 veterans, and 13.5% of residents were born outside the United States.

Retail also matters here. The 2022 Census figure for total retail sales in Collierville is about $1.24 billion, or $24,241 per resident, and the Carriage Crossing shopping mall sits in town. A seller who can state both the town and county bills clearly gives a buyer an easy number to compare.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Collierville tax when you sell the house?
sections.html:
The title company settles any open balance at closing, so get payoff figures from both the Shelby County Trustee and the town's tax department ahead of time. The Trustee says each payoff is verified on the day the money arrives, with the owner liable for charges through that day.

Read the purchase contract and settlement statement to see who covers the current year's tax.

If you are behind, interest piles up each month from March 1 and a lien stays on the parcel until you clear the balance. Calling the town and the Trustee for a payoff is the right first move.

faqs.q: When are Collierville property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due the first Monday of October and can be paid without interest until the end of February. For the bill now outstanding, that means the deadline falls at the end of February 2027, and March 1 starts the delinquent period.

faqs.q: What is the Collierville town property tax rate?
faqs.a: The town's Taxes page gives $1.62 for each $100 of assessed value. At the state's 25% residential ratio, a $100,000 appraisal yields $405.00 of town tax. Shelby County bills its own rate on top of that, and the Trustee or the Assessor can tell you what it is for your parcel.

faqs.q: What interest applies if I pay a Collierville tax bill late?
faqs.a: Interest is 1.5% per month, or 18% per year, beginning March 1 on unpaid base tax. The Shelby County Trustee lists the same rate for Collierville, Arlington, Lakeland, Millington, Memphis and the county itself.

faqs.q: Is the informal review the same as an appeal?
faqs.a: No. The Shelby County Assessor says an informal review is an opportunity to share information so values reflect market value, and it resolves many disputes. The formal appeal goes to the Shelby County Board of Equalization, usually by the last working day of June.

faqs.q: Whom should I call with a Collierville tax question?
faqs.a: Call the town's tax department at 901-457-2281 for town billing, and Shelby County Trustee customer service at (901) 222-0200 for county balances. For value questions, contact the Shelby County Assessor, or the Board of Equalization at 901-222-7300 once you are ready to file a formal appeal.
